review_candidates.title: Head of Sales and Business Development
review_candidates.description: EXOSYSTEMS | Medical Devices, Digital Health & Pharma Partnerships About EXOSYSTEMS EXOSYSTEMS is working to make neuromuscular function easier to measure and understand. Founded in 2017 as a spin-off from Korea’s Electronics and Telecommunications Research Institute (ETRI), we develop wearable sensors that measure neuromuscular biosignals and AI that translates these measurements into digital biomarkers. Backed by leading strategic and financial investors including Daewoong Pharmaceutical, NAVER, SBI Investment, and KDB Capital, we are building on the use of our technology in Korean healthcare settings while expanding international opportunities and pharma partnerships. Our next stage is to turn product adoption into repeatable commercial growth and develop high-value applications with clinical and research partners. The Role We are looking for a Head of Sales and Business Development to lead commercial growth across our medical device and digital health portfolio. Reporting to the CEO, you will set commercial priorities and lead execution across Korea, selected international markets, and pharma partnerships. This is a hands-on leadership role: you will personally win new business, lead key negotiations, and develop the commercial team. Your initial focus will be to grow revenue from existing products while advancing a focused set of international and pharma opportunities. You will agree growth targets, budgets, and hiring priorities with the CEO and build the team’s capabilities as the business grows. This role requires domestic and international travel as needed. What You'll Do Grow the domestic business. Win new hospital and customer accounts, expand use within existing accounts, and improve distributor performance. Personally lead priority opportunities from initial engagement through negotiation and contract execution. Develop international business. Pinpoint priority markets, customer segments, and go-to-market strategies. Establish local partnerships and lead commercial negotiations, ensuring commitments align with product readiness, clinical evidence, and market access requirements. Build pharma strategy and partnerships.  Identify opportunities where our digital biomarkers can solve research bottlenecks for pharma, biotech, and CRO partners. Collaborate with internal technical and clinical teams to define use cases, evidence requirements, and commercial terms, driving promising leads to closed agreements. Own commercial performance. Oversee pricing strategies, revenue forecasting, budgets, and cash flow predictability. Leverage customer feedback and market data to continuously refine priorities and resource allocation. Build and lead the business organization. Recruit, mentor, and develop a high-performing commercial team. Establish clear KPIs across sales, marketing, and partnerships, fostering seamless cross-functional alignment with technical, clinical, quality, and regulatory teams. Your First Priorities (First 3-6 Months) Grow revenue from existing products by winning new customers and increasing use within current accounts. Focus our international business development efforts on a highly targeted set of well-defined opportunities. Advance selected pharma discussions toward funded pilots or commercial agreements, with clear scopes, decision-makers, and timelines. Implement robust pipeline management, reliable forecasting, and a regular review cadence for the business team. What You'll Bring A track record of personally winning new customers and closing commercial agreements in medical devices, digital health, or a related healthcare field, with clear responsibility for revenue results. Extensive experience driving international business development and leading complex commercial negotiations with overseas stakeholders. The technical and business acumen to understand clinical/pharma research needs and translate them into credible, actionable partner proposals. Exceptional leadership skills with sound judgment in pricing, budgeting, and resource allocation. Professional bilingual proficiency in Korean (for domestic execution and team leadership) and English (for international negotiations). Practical experience using AI tools and commercial data to research markets, assess partners, and improve proposals, with sound judgment in verifying outputs. Preferred Experience Experience building a commercial team from the ground up or leading zero-to-one business development in a startup environment. Successful track record of market entry in international healthcare sectors, particularly the United States. Hands-on experience executing partnerships involving digital biomarkers, decentralized clinical trials, or patient monitoring. How to Apply Apply through LinkedIn or email your CV or LinkedIn profile to job@exosystems.io. review_candidates.description: Sé parte de las experiencias que inspiran a descubrir el Perú En Andean creamos experiencias extraordinarias en los destinos más fascinantes del Perú. Cada detalle que cuidamos tiene un propósito: sorprender y engreír a nuestros huéspedes. Hoy buscamos personas apasionadas por la organización, la excelencia y el trabajo en equipo, que quieran crecer junto a nosotros. Tu propósito Liderar integralmente la operación del hotel, siendo el principal anfitrión de la unidad y asegurando que cada huésped viva una experiencia cálida, personalizada y memorable. Gestionar los resultados del negocio, desarrollar al equipo y garantizar el cumplimiento de los estándares de servicio y operación. Lo que harás Liderar y supervisar la operación diaria del hotel, asegurando el correcto funcionamiento de todas las áreas y el cumplimiento de los estándares de servicio. Ser el principal anfitrión de la unidad, recibiendo, acompañando y manteniendo contacto cercano con los huéspedes durante su estadía. Anticipar las necesidades de los huéspedes, atender solicitudes y resolver oportunamente cualquier incidencia, asegurando una experiencia personalizada. Mantener presencia activa en los diferentes espacios del hotel, acompañando los servicios y verificando que cada detalle esté cuidado. Liderar, motivar y desarrollar al equipo de trabajo, promoviendo una cultura de servicio, colaboración y excelencia. Supervisar los indicadores operativos y financieros del hotel, gestionando presupuestos, costos, ingresos y rentabilidad. Coordinar con las diferentes áreas para asegurar la disponibilidad de recursos, instalaciones, insumos y personal. Identificar oportunidades de mejora en la operación y experiencia del huésped, implementando acciones que eleven los estándares del hotel. Gestionar la relación con proveedores y aliados locales, asegurando el abastecimiento y continuidad de los servicios. Coordinar con las áreas corporativas el seguimiento de objetivos, proyectos e iniciativas de la unidad. ¿Qué te hará destacar? Profesional en Administración Hotelera, Hotelería, Turismo, Administración o carreras afines. Experiencia mínima de 5 años en el sector hotelero, con al menos 2 años liderando operaciones o equipos. Experiencia en hoteles boutique, hoteles de destino o establecimientos con atención personalizada (deseable). Experiencia directa en gestión de huéspedes, recepción y resolución de incidencias. Conocimiento de indicadores hoteleros, presupuestos, costos y rentabilidad. Manejo de sistemas hoteleros y herramientas de gestión. Inglés avanzado. Liderazgo cercano, vocación de servicio y excelentes habilidades de comunicación. Capacidad para tomar decisiones, resolver situaciones imprevistas y gestionar equipos de manera autónoma. Disponibilidad para trabajar en el destino asignado. ¿Por qué elegir Andean? Oportunidades de aprendizaje y desarrollo profesional. Línea de carrera dentro de la organización. Un ambiente de trabajo cercano, colaborativo y orientado a la excelencia. La oportunidad de contribuir a crear experiencias únicas e inolvidables para nuestros huéspedes. Formar parte de una empresa peruana reconocida por su propuesta de turismo y hospitalidad de lujo. En Andean promovemos un entorno de trabajo diverso, inclusivo y libre de discriminación. Valoramos el talento, las capacidades y el potencial de cada persona, en cumplimiento de la Ley N.° 26772.

review_candidates.title: Fixed Plant Fitter
review_candidates.description: Job description: Who we are We’re a bold team with a bright future; and we’re looking for people who want to be part of it. Evolution Mining is a premier global gold company operating six mines across Australia and Canada. We’re transforming mines and uplifting careers. We’ve extended the mine life of our Ernest Henry Operations to 2040 and doubled its ore reserves. We took our Cowal Gold Operations underground in just seven years. We’re transforming our Red Lake Operations, restoring it as a premier Canadian gold mine. That kind of ambition creates careers, not just jobs. When we asked our people what they enjoy most about working at Evolution, two things came up across every site: career growth and the quality of the people. Here, you’ll work alongside people who care, who push one another to be better, with leaders who are there to support you. What’s the opportunity? Build your future with a long-life operation that is investing heavily in growth, reliability and performance. This is an opportunity to join the Processing Maintenance team at Mungari and play a hands-on role in keeping critical plant equipment operating safely and efficiently. As a Fixed Plant Fitter, you'll be part of a team that values strong workmanship, practical problem solving and accountability. You'll work across a diverse processing operation, contributing to maintenance activities that directly support production outcomes while ensuring safety remains the priority every day. Based at our Mungari Operations and reporting to the Mechanical Maintenance Supervisor, you'll: Keep the processing plant operating reliably by carrying out planned, preventative and breakdown maintenance activities. Support shutdown execution and maintenance improvement initiatives that maximise plant availability. Identify equipment defects, hazards and maintenance issues before they impact production. Maintain high standards of safety, housekeeping and workmanship across all tasks. Contribute to a collaborative team environment where reliability, accountability and continuous improvement matter. Why Mungari Operations? Mungari is a cornerstone asset in our portfolio, with a mine life to at least 2038. It’s operationally diverse, with opportunities to work on the surface or underground and a great team of people who care. Our recent expansion of the processing plant has more than doubled processing capacity from 2 million to 4.2 million tonnes per year. With open pit and processing all on one site, the operational diversity is ideal for uplifting careers. This opportunity is offered on an 8:6 roster working 10-hour days and is only available to those residing in the Kalgoorlie region. For those considering relocation, Kalgoorlie offers the benefits of a thriving mining community, excellent amenities and a strong local lifestyle. The future here is bright; you could be part of it. What we offer you We support, develop and reward you to ensure you have a bright future. Here’s how we back that up: An attractive residential roster that supports work-life balance (8:6) Quarterly performance bonuses Employee share scheme – have a real stake in the company's success Competitive live-local incentives and allowances Relocation support (where applicable) Salary packaging opportunities Life insurance and income protection Attractive parental leave benefits (18 weeks) Recognition program Study assistance Referral bonuses Discounted health insurance Does this sound like you? Trade qualification as a Mechanical Fitter or similar recognised mechanical trade. Current C Class Driver's Licence. Residential in Kalgoorlie-Boulder or willing to relocate permanently. Experience maintaining fixed plant equipment within mining, mineral processing or heavy industrial environments. Strong commitment to safety and achieving high standards of workmanship. Demonstrated problem-solving skills and a focus on equipment reliability. Basic computer literacy. Ability to work effectively within a team environment built on respect and accountability. Highly regarded: High Risk Work Licence including CN, LF, DG and/or WP classes. Experience with Metso crushers and Warman pumps. Previous gold processing plant maintenance experience. Ready to create your career highlight with us? As our name suggests, change and evolution are in our DNA. If you’d like to work with a team that turns challenges into opportunities and delivers on its bold ambitions, we want to hear from you. Find out more about us at our Careers site. Bold team. Bright future.

review_candidates.title: Events Manager
review_candidates.description: Department: Managed Services Location: San Diego, CA Compensation: $75,000 / year Description ORGANIZATIONAL BACKGROUND The New Children’s Museum’s (NCM) mission is to spark creativity, exploration, and a sense of belonging through interactive art experiences. Located in downtown San Diego, The New Children’s Museum collaborates with contemporary artists to design and create art installations and educational programs for children. Our vision is to be the most innovative, most loved, most inspiring, and most sustainable children’s museum in the world. Our interactive art installations and hands-on art programming provide creative and educational experiences for children and families. We work with artists to reimagine our spaces so that there is always something "new" to discover with every visit. As a nonprofit institution, we rely on daily admissions, memberships, and community support to fund our daily operations. POSITION OVERVIEW The Events Manager is responsible for the planning, coordination, execution, and evaluation of all internal and external events hosted at The New Children's Museum. This position oversees the Museum's event rental program, including corporate events, private celebrations, nonprofit events, and community gatherings, while supporting institutional events such as donor cultivation events, member programs, and fundraising initiatives. The Events Manager serves as the primary liaison for event clients from initial inquiry through event completion, ensuring exceptional customer service and a seamless guest experience. This position works collaboratively with departments across the Museum including Visitor Experience, Facilities, Security, Education, Curatorial, Marketing and Communications, Development, and Finance to coordinate logistics, staffing, budgets, and event operations. The ideal candidate is an organized, service-oriented professional with exceptional project management skills, strong business acumen, and experience managing multiple events simultaneously in a dynamic, fast-paced environment. RESPONSIBILITIES Event Sales & Client Management Serve as the primary point of contact for prospective and confirmed event clients. Manage the event sales process from inquiry through contract execution, planning, event delivery, and post-event follow-up. Conduct site tours for prospective clients. Prepare event proposals, estimates, contracts, invoices, and event orders. Develop strong relationships with clients, vendors, caterers, event planners, and community partners. Maintain a high level of customer service while ensuring Museum policies and operational requirements are met. Event Planning & Logistics Plan, coordinate, and execute all Museum rental events including: Corporate events, Private celebrations, Community events, Nonprofit events, Film/photo shoots, Museum-hosted special events. Develop comprehensive event timelines and production schedules. Coordinate room setups, furniture layouts, equipment needs, signage, parking, loading access, security, custodial services, and vendor logistics. Ensure all event details are communicated effectively across Museum departments. Oversee event setup, execution, and breakdown. Serve as the Manager on Duty for assigned events. Revenue Generation Manage and grow the Museum's earned revenue event business. Develop strategies to increase event bookings and maximize revenue opportunities. Monitor pricing, utilization, and profitability of rental spaces. Identify new event offerings and revenue-generating opportunities aligned with the Museum's mission. Collaborate with Marketing and Communications to promote rental opportunities and event services. Internal Event Support Partner with the Advancement team to coordinate fundraising events, donor receptions, sponsor activations, and stewardship events. Support Museum exhibitions opening celebrations, member events, and community programs. Coordinate logistics for Board meetings and institutional gatherings as needed. Operations & Administration Develop and maintain event policies, procedures, and operational standards. Maintain the Museum's master event calendar. Coordinate staffing needs with Visitor Experience, Security, Facilities, and other departments. Manage event inventory and equipment. Ensure compliance with Museum safety policies and risk management procedures. Maintain accurate event records and financial documentation. Financial Management Develop and manage the annual Events budget. Monitor event revenue and expenses. Process contracts, deposits, invoices, and final billing. Ensure event profitability Recommend operational improvements to increase efficiency and revenue. Leadership & Collaboration Supervise and support the Event Lead and on-call Event staff Recruit, train, and schedule event staff Foster a collaborative, customer-focused culture. Work cross-functionally to ensure successful event execution throughout the Museum. Evaluation & Reporting Establish key performance indicators (KPIs) for event success. Analyze booking trends, customer satisfaction, revenue performance, and operational effectiveness. Collect client feedback and recommend improvements. Prepare monthly and annual reports for senior leadership. Perform other duties as assigned. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS Education & Experience Bachelor's degree in Hospitality, Event Management, Business Administration, Marketing, Nonprofit Management, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience. Minimum of three (3) years of progressively responsible event management experience. Experience managing multiple complex events simultaneously. Experience preparing budgets and managing event financial performance. Experience working with event management software and CRM systems preferred. Knowledge, Skills & Abilities Exceptional organizational and project management skills. Strong customer service and relationship management skills. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Ability to prioritize competing deadlines in a fast-paced environment. Strong negotiation and problem-solving skills. Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, including Outlook, Word, Excel, and Teams. Ability to work collaboratively with diverse internal and external stakeholders. Commitment to providing an exceptional guest experience. Familiarity with event-related permitting, insurance, and safety compliance requirements. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Experience working in museums, cultural institutions, nonprofits, or attractions. Experience with event booking software. Familiarity with Canva, Adobe Creative Suite, or marketing platforms. Knowledge of catering and hospitality operations. Bilingual in English and Spanish. PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS This position regularly requires standing, walking, and moving throughout museum gallery, event, and outdoor spaces for extended periods while planning, coordinating, and overseeing events. The role involves frequent interaction with clients, vendors, museum staff, and the public in active and dynamic indoor and outdoor settings. Employees in this position may be required to lift, carry, push, or pull equipment and supplies weighing up to 25 pounds. Work is performed in a museum environment that requires flexibility and the ability to operate in a collaborative, fast-paced setting. Evening, weekend, and holiday availability is required based on the Museum’s event schedule. The employee must be able to perform essential job duties with or without reasonable accommodation. BENEFITS Medical, dental, and vision insurance Flexible Spending Account (FSA) 403(b) retirement plan with a 3% employer match after one year 10 vacation days annually 10 paid sick days (2 available immediately) 12 paid holidays 3 floating holidays The New Children's Museum is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a team that reflects the diverse communities and families we serve. We welcome candidates of all backgrounds and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status, or any other status protected under federal, state, or local law. Reasonable accommodations are available upon request.
